Standard: In forward flight (greater than 45 KGS), the air vehicle's spiral mode stability as indicated by the variation of bank angle with time is linear or the time to double in bank angle is greater than 12 seconds. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct analysis to assess the spiral mode stability as indicated by the bank angle time to double as specified in MIL-DTL-32742, Spiral Stability paragraph for each air vehicle configuration and loading within the SFE. A linear variation of bank angle with time following lateral pulse input regardless of the time to double is considered compliant. The initiating pulse input should be just large enough to generate a roll disturbance. Spiral mode stability is either stable (bank angle returns to trim), neutral (bank angle remains at new position), or divergent (bank angle continuously increases). Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct piloted simulation and evaluation to assess the spiral mode stability as indicated by the bank angle time to double as specified in MIL-DTL-32742, Spiral Stability paragraph for each air vehicle configuration and loading within the SFE. A linear variation of bank angle with time following lateral pulse input regardless of the time to double is considered compliant. The initiating pulse input should be just large enough to generate a roll disturbance. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Conduct flight test to assess the spiral mode stability as indicated by the bank angle time to double as specified in MIL-DTL-32742, Spiral Stability paragraph for selected combinations of air vehicle configuration and loading within the SFE. A linear variation of bank angle with time following lateral pulse input regardless of the time to double is considered compliant. The initiating pulse input should be just large enough to generate a roll disturbance.
